name: Emo (Chinese slang)
blurb: Chinese internet slang for feeling down or blue, as in 我emo了 ("I'm feeling emo")
title: Emo Meaning in Chinese Slang: What Does 我emo了 Mean?
description: On the Chinese internet, emo means feeling low or sad; 我emo了 is "I'm feeling down". Borrowed from the emo rock genre, it took off in 2021.
h1: What does emo mean in Chinese slang?
answer: On the Chinese internet, emo means feeling low, sad or a bit defeated. The standard phrase is 我emo了 (wǒ emo le, "I'm feeling emo"), close to "I'm feeling down". It is usually self-mocking and does not mean real depression. The word is borrowed from emo, the emotional rock genre that grew out of the Washington, D.C. hardcore punk scene in the mid-1980s, and it spread across Chinese social media in 2021.

sections.h: From a music genre to 我emo了
body: In English, emo is short for emotional hardcore (emocore): a style that began in the Washington, D.C. hardcore punk scene in the mid-1980s, keeping the loud guitars but adding personal, emotional lyrics. Later the word also covered fans of the music and their dark, moody look.

Chinese speakers kept only the "sad, low" part of that meaning and turned emo into a verb and an adjective: 我emo了 ("I'm emo now"), 有点emo ("a bit emo"). In 2021 Chinese media such as China News Service reported that 我emo了 was everywhere online, the next catchphrase after 破防 (pòfáng). Any small setback could be a reason to "emo for a moment".

ul: 「四六级又没过，我emo了。」 (Failed the English exam again. I'm feeling emo.)
「下雨天还要加班到十点，有点emo。」 (Rain, and overtime until ten. A bit emo.)
「别emo了，出来吃火锅。」 (Stop moping, come out for hot pot.)
「一到深夜就开始emo。」 (Every night after midnight I start getting emo.)
「这首歌太emo了。」 (This song is so sad.)

body: It works on its own as a verb (我emo了), with 有点 "a bit" or 太 "too", and in compounds such as emo时间 ("emo hour", the late-night sad mood).

body: Chinese emo is casual and playful, fine with friends and in posts; in formal writing say 心情低落 ("in low spirits"). Teasing someone with 你又emo了 ("emo again?") is usually friendly, but it can sound dismissive if they are really struggling.

body.note: If low mood lasts a long time and affects sleep or daily life, it is more than a passing "emo" moment. Talk to someone you trust or look for professional help.

faq.q: How do you pronounce emo in Chinese?
faq.a: Most people say it the English way, "EE-moh". Some spell out the letters E-M-O. The meaning is the same.

faq.q: Does 我emo了 mean someone is depressed?
faq.a: No. It describes a passing low mood and is often a joke at one's own expense. Depression is a medical condition that needs a professional diagnosis.

faq.q: Is Chinese emo the same as the emo music genre?
faq.a: It borrows the name. The genre is a style of rock from the mid-1980s Washington, D.C. punk scene; the Chinese slang keeps only the sense of feeling sad.
